title: Breakfast on the Beach, Peter Restored
overview: The risen Jesus meets several followers at a lake in Galilee, feeds them breakfast, and gives Peter a fresh start after his earlier failure.

parts.label: Back to Fishing (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Seven of Jesus' followers have gone home to Galilee and returned to their old trade while they wait to see what comes next. A whole night of work brings in nothing.

parts.label: A Stranger on the Shore (vv. 4-8)
parts.note: A man on the beach tells them where to throw the net and it suddenly fills, echoing the earlier day when Jesus first called these fishermen to 'fish for people.' The disciple Jesus loved recognizes him first, and Peter jumps into the shallow water to reach him sooner.

parts.label: Breakfast by the Fire (vv. 9-14)
parts.note: Jesus already has fish cooking and hands out bread and fish, a quiet sign that he is really alive and still looking after them. The exact count of 153 fish has prompted many symbolic guesses, often that the catch pictures the many people the disciples would one day reach, but no one knows for sure.

parts.label: Three Questions for Peter (vv. 15-19)
parts.note: Peter had denied knowing Jesus three times beside a charcoal fire, so now, beside another charcoal fire, Jesus asks three times whether Peter loves him and each time hands him the job of caring for his followers, 'my sheep.' The words about stretching out his hands point to how Peter would die, and early Christian tradition says he was crucified in Rome.

parts.label: What About Him? (vv. 20-23)
parts.note: When Peter asks what will happen to the disciple Jesus loved, Jesus says that is not Peter's concern: 'You must follow me.' The writer corrects a rumor that this disciple would never die, which many scholars think came up because he was very old or had already died when this was written.

parts.label: The Closing Witness (vv. 24-25)
parts.note: The book names this beloved disciple as the source behind its account, and a group speaking as 'we' vouches that his testimony is true. It ends by admitting it tells only a small part of what Jesus did.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether Jesus' charge to Peter gives him and those after him a special leadership role over the whole church, as Catholics hold, or mainly restores Peter personally after his denials, as most Protestants read it.
think: What do you think makes a fresh start after a serious failure feel real, rather than just words?
